notes: *have warmth* is divided under rule 43: the clause is not verbless but `חַם`'s own lexeme is written by *warmth*, so the dative `לְ` is what makes the clause possessive and takes *have*, with the suffix taking *they* — the `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* pattern.
Italic *alone* answers to no morpheme and is added (rules 7, 30); the competing reading gives it to `אֶחָד` as a second realization under rule 25.
*together* is kept with `יִשְׁכְּבוּ` as part of the English verb's rendering (rule 44), as with `חֹבֵק` → *foldeth ... together* in ECC.4.5; the competing reading marks it added.
`אֵיךְ` holds an English word of its own, so the fronted *can* stays with the verb (rule 17's second limit).
